kind: Test fixture ownership lifecycle; no production protocol, IO ledger or command change

states.REGISTERED: Static exact-root record exists before scheduling coordinator. No session execution if admission closes.
states.CREATING/CREATED/RESTORING: Creation entered and exact session captured in Main before starting restore/crossing a cancellable return.
states.ACQUIRING/ACQUIRED: Acquisition entered in Main; exact returned lease captured before context/timeout return. Throw without lease is unconfirmed, no abandonment/retry.
states.RETIRE_QUEUED/RETIRING/RETIRED: One retire attempt; retirementConfirmed is set only after actual synchronous call normally returns inside Main.
states.RELEASE_QUEUED/RELEASING/RELEASED: One release attempt only after retirementConfirmed. releaseConfirmed only after actual normal return inside IO. Failure is partial/unknown, never retried.
states.ABANDON_QUEUED/ABANDONING/ABANDONED: Only before acquisition ever entered; actual abandon normal return inside Main confirms session stop.
states.NO_SESSION: Coordinator/creation never entered, so there is no created Session/lease to stop. Constructor entered but failed to return an object is not declared clean.

rules: Never release raw/child frozen handles in an unconditional finally after retirement failure or unknown return.
On cleanup unknown, keep exact actual objects strongly and remain inside real untimed instrumentation/JUnit wait. No recreated session/lease, guessed outcome, JSON-only substitute or process exit.

A pending cleanup can wake waits only when actual confirmation is recorded. A failed retire/release has no retry/unblock/clear API; Root must preserve the process and original objects for explicit followup.
First action/assertion failure remains primary; verification/retire/release/diagnostic/interrupt failures are added as suppressed, not replacements.
Counter/phase, cancelled Job and signal file are not proof of actor exit. JUnit rule checks actual worker exit and cleanup facts.

Every Native fixture uses default untimed wait and owner rule. Fake-resource JVM tests alone inject a throwing observation wait; even that cannot bypass the Native JUnit outer guard for unresolved real records.

No new production owner ledger. Test registry key is exact canonical coordination directory, preventing a new test Session replacing an unresolved owner. No runtime test UUID is assigned by this source work.

Actual JUnit guard and exact body Thread are both retained. Guard requests local body cancellation once on first interrupt, closes new enrollment, and records later interrupts; no forced JUnit completion while owner remains unconfirmed.
NativeExpectations: Normal execution retires once then releases once, preserving existing success or original body failure semantics.
Cancel at Main create/acquire return preserves exact original session/lease; no original object is lost at withContext/withTimeout return.
Retire throw/partial retirement leaves release call count0 and original raw gate held; source/root/candidate/key unchanged; JUnit stays live.
Release throw records partial/unknown close with call count1, keeps exact owner/objects/context and does not retry or mark released.
Interrupt during pending retire/release does not end instrumentation/JUnit; further interrupts are recorded, no duplicate cleanup or replacement Session.
If actual in-flight cleanup later confirms, guard/body thread complete and original assertion/cancellation propagates; no forced success.
If no confirmation can arrive after failure, keep original process/context. Do not force-stop instrumentation as automatic timeout cleanup or replay a selector; Parent owns explicit safe followup.
currentEvidence: Portable JVM14 plus PSI5 only; actual Android Session/raw locks/Keystore and prior9 Native selectors still unexecuted.
